title: Microsoft Edge: security update alerts with a severity threshold in the Edge management service
notes: claim 51: severity major on a rationale: risk rating lowered to minor; ratings are judgements and cannot hold a page
summary: Hold: the briefing says the browser check-in policy has no documented admin UI, but Microsoft publishes its Group Policy setting. It also asserts that alerts depend on the diagnostic-data choice without documentation establishing that dependency. The roadmap dates, notification default and service access path are supported.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; controls[0].note; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Administrators can configure a minimum severity threshold that generates alerts for new Edge updates with security fixes meeting or exceeding it, including zero-day fixes.
claims.quote: You can configure a minimum severity threshold for security update alerts. Alerts are generated when a newly released Microsoft Edge update includes security fixes that meet or exceed the configured severity level, including zero-day vulnerability fixes.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the aim as identifying updates needing attention while avoiding routine-release notifications.
claims.quote: This helps organizations quickly identify updates that may require attention, while avoiding unnecessary notifications for routine releases.

claims.claim: Security update alerts appear in the monitoring dashboard.
claims.quote: When a new security update becomes available, an alert is displayed in the monitoring dashboard with information about the release, its severity, the security vulnerabilities addressed, and the devices that may require updating.

claims.claim: An alert shows the released Edge version.
claims.quote: Edge version released - The Microsoft Edge version containing the security update and the date the update was released.

claims.claim: An alert shows the update release date.
claims.quote: Edge version released - The Microsoft Edge version containing the security update and the date the update was released.

claims.claim: An alert shows the highest security severity among the vulnerabilities addressed.
claims.quote: Severity level - The highest security severity associated with vulnerabilities addressed in the release.

claims.claim: An alert lists the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures addressed.
claims.quote: CVEs addressed - The Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) addressed by the release, helping you understand the security issues resolved by the update.

claims.where: What's changing: alert contents; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: An alert shows the number of affected managed devices by Edge channel.

claims.claim: An alert shows the latest available versions for Stable, Extended Stable, Beta, Dev and Canary.
claims.quote: Latest available version by channel - The current version available for each Microsoft Edge channel, including Stable, Extended Stable, Beta, Dev, and Canary.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: From an alert, an administrator can review update details and take action to bring managed devices to the latest secure version.
claims.quote: From the alert, you can review the update details, understand which CVEs were addressed, identify affected devices across channels, and take action to help ensure managed devices are running the latest secure version of Microsoft Edge.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents neither the threshold's navigation path nor an API for configuring it.
claims.quote: Searched: "severity threshold" "security update alerts" "Settings"; "Edge management service" "severity" "Graph"; threshold Edge policy. Opened Monitoring dashboard, configuration policies, Graph Edge API /beta; no threshold path or API.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not list the selectable security-alert severity levels.
claims.quote: Searched: "security update alerts" "threshold" configure Microsoft Edge policy; "severity threshold" "security update alerts" "Settings". Opened Monitoring dashboard and read the returned Stable release-note passage; neither enumerates selectable levels.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; Governance controls; licensing notes
claims.claim: Access to the Edge management service requires the Microsoft Edge Administrator role.

claims.claim: No API equivalent of opening the Edge management service admin-centre experience is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Graph" "Edge management service" access API. Opened configuration policies and Graph Edge API /beta; Graph documents IE-mode site-list operations, not an operation opening this admin-centre experience.

claims.claim: Setting EdgeManagementEnabled to 0 or disabled disables browser check-in with the Edge management service for configuration policies.
claims.quote: To disable the checking in with the Edge management service you can set the EdgeManagementEnabled policy to 0 or disabled.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: browser check-in row
claims.claim: The EdgeManagementEnabled browser check-in control has no documented admin UI.
claims.quote: GP name: Microsoft Edge management enabled; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Manageability; GP ADMX file name: MSEdge.admx
claims.fix: Replace controls[2].ui null and the matching table gap with surface 'Group Policy (ADMX)', path 'Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Manageability > Microsoft Edge management enabled', and docs https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/edgemanagementenabled. Qualify this UI as Windows-only.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed whether EdgeManagementEnabled governs monitoring data or security update alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: "EdgeManagementEnabled" policy group policy; "Edge management service" "security update alerts" "data collection". Opened EdgeManagementEnabled, configuration policies and Monitoring dashboard; no passage explicitly connects this policy to alert telemetry.

claims.claim: The service lists Windows, macOS, iOS and Android as supported operating systems.
claims.quote: You must be using one of the following supported operating systems: Windows, macOS, iOS, or Android.

claims.claim: The Edge management service is currently unavailable to customers with GCC plans.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Edge management service is currently not available to customers with GCC plans.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enable version monitoring is mandatory to view device insights on the dashboard and provides necessary diagnostic data.
claims.quote: To view device insights on this page, you must first turn on the toggle to Enable version monitoring. This is a mandatory step to ensure that Microsoft Edge receives the necessary diagnostic data

claims.claim: The without-URL monitoring option sends optional diagnostic data but disables URL and per-page usage collection.
claims.quote: It also disables the UrlDiagnosticDataEnabled policy to not send data about page URLs and per-page usage.

claims.claim: The with-URL monitoring option sends optional diagnostic data including page URLs and per-page usage.
claims.quote: It also enables the UrlDiagnosticDataEnabled policy to send data about page URLs and per-page usage to help make browsing and search better.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, first bullet
claims.claim: Security update alerts depend on the version-monitoring diagnostic-data choice rather than adding to it.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Edge" "monitoring" "alerts" "diagnostic"; "Edge management service" "security update alerts" "data collection". Opened Monitoring dashboard and configuration policies; no text states this alert-specific dependency or data boundary.
claims.fix: Remove 'Alerts depend on that choice rather than adding to it, but' and start the remaining clause 'The Learn page does not say that alerts specifically require this toggle, so confirm it.' The current assertion also conflicts with the uncertainty stated in Open questions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, second bullet
claims.claim: A device's update information is deleted after it has sent no data for 30 days.
claims.quote: If a device has not sent data for 30 days, then the update information for that device will be deleted from the Edge management service.

claims.quote: Force auto restart when device is idle: This action automatically restarts the users' browsers to apply the latest update when their device is detected as idle.

claims.claim: Forcing a browser restart when idle may cause loss of content input.
claims.quote: Note: This may cause loss of content input.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The sources do not document an alert automatically triggering a device update or restart action.
claims.quote: Searched: "Edge" "security update alerts" "automatically" restart. Opened Monitoring dashboard and configuration policies; read MC1458480. Alerts provide information; dashboard restart actions are described as actions administrators choose.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document email or other delivery channels for these security update alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: "Edge management service" "security update alerts" "email". Opened Monitoring dashboard and configuration policies; the feature passage documents dashboard alerts, not email, Message center delivery or recipient configuration.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The licensing model for security update alerts is unknown because Microsoft has not published its licence requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Edge management service" licensing pricing monitoring; "Microsoft Edge management service" "license" "monitoring dashboard". Opened Monitoring dashboard and configuration policies; neither states alert licensing, pricing or a counted-device licence.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The service prerequisite list names an Edge version, administrator role and operating system but no licence.
claims.quote: You must have Microsoft Edge 115.0.1901.7 or greater installed. You must be a Microsoft Edge Administrator to access the experience in Microsoft 365 Admin Center (Note: GDAP roles are currently not fully supported).

claims.claim: Creating an Intune-type configuration policy, a separate operation from alerts, requires an Intune licence.
claims.quote: Choose whether you would like to create an Intune type policy or Cloud (you must have an Intune license to be able to create an Intune policy).

claims.claim: No meter is documented for this feature at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Edge management service" licensing pricing monitoring; "Edge management service" "security update alerts" "license". Opened Monitoring dashboard and configuration policies; neither documents an alert consumption meter or rate.

claims.claim: A low severity threshold preserves the notification volume of the existing all-updates experience.
claims.quote: Searched: "security update alerts" "all updates" threshold Edge. Opened Monitoring dashboard; read the Stable release-note passage and MC1458480. Sources describe security-fix filtering but do not say a low threshold reproduces all-update notifications.
claims.fix: Replace 'a low threshold keeps the volume of the current all-updates experience, and a higher one narrows alerts to the more serious fixes, including zero-day fixes' with 'a configured threshold limits alerts to updates containing security fixes that meet or exceed that severity level, including zero-day fixes'.

claims.claim: The new alerting control reads nothing new by itself.
claims.quote: Searched: "Edge management service" "security update alerts" "data collection"; "Microsoft Edge" "monitoring" "alerts" "diagnostic". Opened Monitoring dashboard and configuration policies; neither establishes that alerts introduce no additional data reads.
claims.fix: Remove 'that reads nothing new by itself' from the risk rationale. Keep the supported statement that MC1458480 preserves the existing all-updates notification experience by default.

claims.claim: Only administrators using the Edge management service see its security update alerts.
claims.quote: You must be a Microsoft Edge Administrator to access the experience in Microsoft 365 Admin Center (Note: GDAP roles are currently not fully supported).

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, third bullet
claims.claim: The checklist tells administrators to check Enable version monitoring and its diagnostic-data option, but the controls table has no corresponding row.
claims.quote: Check whether the Enable version monitoring toggle on the monitoring dashboard is on and which diagnostic data option your privacy team has approved. The table covers only the severity threshold, service access and browser check-in.
claims.fix: The Before rollout step about Enable version monitoring and diagnostic-data selection has no controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the documented explanation in Risk assessment.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout, second bullet
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to consider Recommend restart and Force auto restart when device is idle, but neither control appears in the controls table.
claims.quote: Review affected devices by channel in each alert and decide whether to use Recommend restart or Force auto restart when device is idle for devices that are out of date. Neither action has a controls-table row.
claims.fix: The After rollout step naming the restart actions has no corresponding controls-table rows. Narrow that bullet to 'Review affected devices by channel in each alert.'

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not publish a charge for security update alerts.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Edge management service" licensing pricing monitoring; "Edge management service" "security update alerts" "license". Opened Monitoring dashboard and configuration policies; no alert price is stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not state which user licences, if any, are required for a device to be counted.
claims.quote: Searched: "Microsoft Edge management service" "license" "monitoring dashboard". Opened Monitoring dashboard and configuration policies; neither gives a user licence prerequisite for device counts.
